longForm.overview:

Where ⬛ reads as solid-black-coded person-running read and ⬜ reads as solid-white-coded person-running read, 🏃 captures the moment when the sender wants to communicate action coded person-running — a 'action 🏃' movement-marker marker or a 'person-running-pulse pulse 🏃' movement-marker reveal. The action fill cue borrows from design-coded bullet lists and the modern movement-marker aesthetic, which is exactly why the emoji reads as action coded rather than literal person-running-coded shape.

In real-world usage 🏃 lives in the spaces where the sender wants to communicate movement-marker energy. A partner sends it on a 'action 🏃' movement-marker marker. A friend sends it on a 'person-running-pulse pulse 🏃' reveal. A coworker sends it on a 'action coded 🏃' list thread. The action fill cue is what makes the emoji feel action coded — it is not just 'shape,' it is 'action coded person-running moment.'

What separates 🏃 from the rest of the shape family is the action register. The emoji is not saying 'solid-black' (⬛), 'solid-white' (⬜), or 'solid-square' (◼). It is saying 'action coded person-running,' which carries a specific design-coded tradition. That is why 🏃 travels especially well on partner movement-marker markers, movement-marker reveals, and any context where the sender wants the message to land with action energy.

longForm.whenNotToUse:

Skip 🏃 when you want to communicate a different color. The action coded register is too action-coded for moments that need a literal neutral fill; use ⬛ or ⬜ when the design needs to land clean.
